title: Build one Claude Project this week
body: Build one Claude Project for your most-repeated writing task this week.
why_matters: At your level, AI is something you use. The shift to compounding starts when you turn one repeated task into a durable surface.
what_to_do: Pick the task you do most often that involves writing or analysis. In Claude, create a Project. Add three things to its instructions: who you are, what good output looks like, what to avoid. Add 2-3 reference docs. Use it for that task all week.
how_to_know: By Friday, you have used the Project at least three times and edited the instructions at least once.

title: Run a 30-minute Friday review
body: Block 30 minutes every Friday to review what AI worked for you that week.
why_matters: Most people use AI without ever looking at where it is working and where it is not. Thirty minutes a week is the smallest investment that produces compounding.
what_to_do: Block 30 minutes Friday afternoon. Open whatever you used AI for this week. Note what worked, what did not, and one thing to try next week.
how_to_know: After three weeks, you have nine notes and at least two describe a habit you have changed.

title: Stop typing the same prompt twice
body: Turn three repeated prompts into reusable Claude Skills.
why_matters: If you have written a prompt more than once, you have identified a Skill. Make it reusable.
what_to_do: Pick three prompts you have used more than once this month. For each, create a Claude Skill (or a saved prompt in your tool of choice). Name them clearly. Use them next week.
how_to_know: Within two weeks you reach for a Skill at least once a day.

title: Pick one personal automation to ship this fortnight
body: Ship one personal automation that runs end-to-end this fortnight.
why_matters: You have the fluency. The next step is shipping something a colleague would notice.
what_to_do: Identify one repetitive personal task. Build it as an n8n workflow or Claude Skill that runs end to end. Document the inputs and outputs in two lines.
how_to_know: In two weeks, the automation has run at least five times without you babysitting it.

title: Teach one teammate the move you use most
body: Teach one teammate your highest-leverage AI move this fortnight.
why_matters: Skill spreads through demonstration, not docs. Pick the colleague who would benefit most and show them.
what_to_do: Pick the AI move that has earned you the most time this month. Block 30 minutes with one colleague. Walk them through it on a real task of theirs.
how_to_know: Within a fortnight, the colleague is using the move on their own work without checking back.

title: Write your AI operating manual
body: Write a one-page personal AI operating manual and share it with two colleagues.
why_matters: You have your own way of working with AI by now. Writing it down is what makes it teachable and durable.
what_to_do: Spend 90 minutes writing a one-page operating manual: which tools for what, your three best Skills, the rules you have learned. Share it with two people.
how_to_know: You can hand the page to a new starter and they can follow it without you in the room.

title: Stretch into agent orchestration
body: Build one multi-step personal agent and run it for two weeks unsupervised.
why_matters: You have outgrown single-prompt work. The next horizon is letting agents take multi-step tasks off your plate.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow with 3+ steps that you currently do by hand. Build it as an agent (Claude Code, n8n, or a custom Claude Skill chain). Run it for two weeks.
how_to_know: You spend less than 10 minutes a week supervising the agent and the output is reliable.

title: Publish a teardown of one workflow
body: Write up one workflow teardown so others can copy your move.
why_matters: At your level, the leverage is in propagating the move, not just doing it. Write it up.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow you have rebuilt with AI. Write a short internal post (or external if relevant): the before, the after, the bits that did not work. Post it.
how_to_know: Within four weeks, two people have copied or adapted the workflow.

title: Rebuild outbound research as your first agent
body: Build an outbound research agent for your top 20 ICP accounts.
why_matters: At your tier, Sales is doing manual research that an agent can do in 1/10 the time and to a higher standard. This is the highest-ROI first agent for almost every RevOps function under 500 people.
what_to_do: Pick your top 20 ICP accounts for the next quarter. Build an agent in Claude (or n8n with Claude as the model) that takes a domain, pulls public signal (news, hires, funding, product changes), and produces a one-page research brief in your team standard format. Run it on the 20 accounts.
how_to_know: Each rep pre-call prep time drops by at least 40% within four weeks. You will see it in their calendars.

title: Move proposal drafting from blank page to assisted
body: Use a Claude Project to assist proposal drafting from your best historical examples.
why_matters: Proposal writing is high-leverage, repetitive, and currently done from scratch. An assisted draft cuts cycle time without losing voice.
what_to_do: Build a Claude Project with your three best historical proposals as references and your sales playbook as instruction. Use it as the starting point for the next 5 proposals. Track time-to-first-draft.
how_to_know: Average time from briefing to first draft drops by 50% within six weeks.

title: Appoint a RevOps AI Owner this month
body: Name a RevOps AI Owner with 20% of their week protected.
why_matters: Without a named owner, AI moves in RevOps stall after the first pilot. The Owner does not need to be senior. They need to be respected and have 20% of their time.
what_to_do: Pick a strong IC (not a manager). Carve out 20% of their week. Their job is to ship and maintain RevOps agents and skills. Tell the team they exist and what they are for.
how_to_know: Within six weeks, the Owner has shipped one new agent or skill that another team member uses weekly.

title: Stop using ChatGPT for prospect data
body: Move all prospect-data AI usage off personal ChatGPT accounts onto a sanctioned tenant.
why_matters: Prospect data in consumer ChatGPT accounts is a real GDPR risk and an unforced error. The fix is simple and free.
what_to_do: This week, audit who in Sales is using personal ChatGPT for prospect research. Move them to your sanctioned Claude or ChatGPT Teams account. Communicate the rule once, in writing.
how_to_know: Within two weeks, no Sales person can produce a recent ChatGPT history on a personal account that includes named prospects.

title: Measure cycle time on one workflow before you change anything else
body: Baseline one RevOps workflow before you AI-ify anything else.
why_matters: Without a baseline, every "AI win" is anecdote. Pick one workflow, time it, then improve.
what_to_do: Choose one repeatable workflow (proposal drafting, lead qualification, call follow-up). Measure end-to-end time for the next 10 instances. Then run any of the Moves above. Re-measure.
how_to_know: You can produce a before/after number that the CFO would believe.

title: Industrialise your best agent with evals
body: Add evals to your most-used RevOps agent and ship changes with confidence.
why_matters: You have shipped one or two agents. The next jump is making them reliable enough to hand off without supervision.
what_to_do: Pick the agent that has the most usage. Write 20 evals covering happy path, edge cases, and failure modes. Run them on every change. Add a logging layer.
how_to_know: You can ship a change to the agent on a Friday and not check in until Monday.

title: Connect your agent to the CRM, not the other way round
body: Wire one CRM trigger to your best agent so it runs in-flow.
why_matters: Most RevOps agents currently sit beside the CRM. The next jump is making the CRM call the agent at the right point in the workflow.
what_to_do: Pick one CRM trigger (new opp created, stage change, owner change). Wire it to your best agent via webhook or n8n. The agent should run in-flow without human prompting.
how_to_know: The agent runs on at least 80% of triggered events without manual kick-off.

title: Re-cut the RevOps team around agents
body: Re-cut RevOps roles around agents instead of alongside them.
why_matters: At this tier, the question is not "what should we automate" but "what shape should the team be". Bend the org chart around the model.
what_to_do: Map every RevOps role against current activities. For each, name the activities that an agent now owns (or should). Re-cut the JDs. Hire the next role as an agent operator, not an analyst.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, at least one role has been redefined with an agent as a primary collaborator.

title: Audit the AI features inside your existing HR stack first
body: Audit the AI features already inside your HR stack before adding more.
why_matters: Most People functions add new AI tools before exploiting what they are already paying for. The AI features inside your HRIS, ATS, and L&D stack are usually 80% of the value with zero procurement.
what_to_do: This week, list every tool People uses. For each, find what AI features exist, are enabled, and are actually used. Disable anything that touches sensitive data and is not sanctioned.
how_to_know: You can produce a one-page map of vertical AI in People, with a named owner per tool.

title: Build a job description agent before any other agent
body: Build a Claude Project that drafts job descriptions from your last 20.
why_matters: JD writing is the People function most repeatable, highest-leverage task. It is also the safest first agent because output is always reviewed.
what_to_do: Build a Claude Project with your last 20 JDs and your DEI guidelines as references. Use it as the starting point for the next 5 JDs. Have hiring managers compare to your old JDs.
how_to_know: JDs ship 60% faster and pass DEI review on first attempt.

title: Set up a People Ops AI Brain
body: Stand up a People Ops knowledge brain in a Claude Project.
why_matters: Your team answers the same policy questions weekly. A central knowledge surface they can query (and that gets better as they query it) compounds.
what_to_do: Build a Claude Project with your handbook, policies, and FAQs. Give the People team access. Track which questions get asked. Refine the corpus monthly.
how_to_know: Within 8 weeks, at least 30% of internal People queries route to the Brain first.

title: Name the owner
body: Pick one accountable lead in writing this week. No committee, no consensus — one named person with a remit and a calendar slot.

title: Write the one-page mandate
body: A single page: what AI is for in this function, what it is not, what success looks like in 90 days. Sign-off from the function head.

title: Carve a budget line
body: Move AI spend from personal cards to a function line item. Even £5k changes the conversation from hobby to programme.

title: Name the five entities that matter
body: Draw the five things your function actually reasons about (accounts, deals, tickets, etc.). Document where each one lives. That is the schema.

title: Audit the shadow drives
body: Find the spreadsheets and shared drives the team actually uses. List them. That is your real data layer — pretending otherwise wastes a year.

title: Stand up one trustworthy view
body: Pick the single most-read report. Make it queryable, accurate, and owned. Use it as the seed for everything else.

title: Sanction one tool
body: Pick one (Copilot, ChatGPT Team, Claude for Work). Buy a team licence. Stop pretending shadow accounts are a strategy.

title: Turn on SSO and audit logs
body: Five-minute config change that turns shadow IT into governed IT. Do this before you do anything clever.

title: Build one internal copilot
body: Wrap your sanctioned model around one workflow with the right prompts and data. Internal users, no external surface. Ships in two weeks.

title: Pick one workflow
body: One workflow, one team, six weeks. Not three pilots. The discipline of one is what unlocks two.

title: Write the playbook
body: Document the workflow with the model in it, step by step. The playbook is what makes it survive the believer leaving.

title: Make AI the default first pass
body: Change the workflow so the human reviews model output rather than producing it. The verb shift is the leverage.

title: Run a 90-minute baseline session
body: Get the whole team into one room. Have them try one prompt each on a real task. The median fluency is now visible.

title: Pair the keenest with the rest
body: Two-person pairings, 30 minutes a week. Cheaper than training, more effective. The teaching is what cements the teacher.

title: Build a shared prompt library
body: A team-owned library of the prompts that work, with one-line provenance. Median person now starts at intermediate, not novice.

title: One-page acceptable use policy
body: Three rules, one page, plain English. What you can paste, what you cannot, who to ask. That is the floor.

title: Approved-tools list with owner
body: A single source of truth for what is sanctioned. Owned by the named lead. Updated quarterly. End of shadow stack.

title: Audit trail and quarterly review
body: Turn on logs in your sanctioned tools. Hold a 30-minute quarterly review of what was used and what went wrong. That is governance.

title: Time three workflows before AI
body: Stopwatch on three real tasks, three people each. That is your baseline. Without it, every ROI claim is anecdote.

title: Track hours saved on one workflow
body: Pick the most-used. Log time-with and time-without for a month. Numbers a CFO accepts in 30 days.

title: Add quality and cycle-time metrics
body: Hours saved is the floor. Add error rate, rework, days-to-completion. Now you can defend the next round of investment.

title: Have leadership use it in public
body: The function head uses AI in the next all-hands, on screen, on a real task. Permission cascades from there.

title: Open a #ai-wins channel
body: A standing place for the team to share what worked. Removes the "is this cheating?" question by making it normal.

title: Make AI fluency a job criterion
body: Put it in the next job description and the next review form. Nothing signals "this is how we work" louder than that.

title: Name an AI sponsor on the leadership team
body: Designate a single executive accountable for AI direction and budget. Without a named sponsor, every initiative stalls at the first cross-functional conflict.

title: Run a 90-minute AI ambition workshop
body: Get the leadership team in a room to write a one-page statement of where AI fits in the next 12 months. Not a strategy — a north star.

title: Publish a one-page AI charter
body: Codify the ambition into 3-5 priority use cases, decision rights, and what is explicitly out of scope. Share it widely.

title: Tie AI initiatives to P&L line items
body: Map each active AI bet to the revenue, cost or risk line it is meant to move. Kill anything you cannot map.

title: Inventory your top 10 data sources
body: List the systems where the data that matters actually lives. Owner, refresh cadence, who can read it. Half a day of work, foundational.

title: Appoint data owners for the top 5 domains
body: Customer, product, finance, ops, people. Each gets one accountable owner. No owner = no quality.

title: Stand up a single source of truth for one domain
body: Pick the highest-value domain and consolidate it into one trusted store. Resist boiling the ocean.

title: Add lineage and quality SLAs to your core pipelines
body: Document where each critical field comes from and define freshness/accuracy targets. Now you can trust your AI outputs.

title: Classify data by sensitivity tier
body: Public, internal, confidential, regulated. Drives every downstream decision about which data can go to which AI tool.

title: Sanction one enterprise AI assistant
body: Pick one (ChatGPT Enterprise, Copilot, Claude for Work) and roll it out broadly. Beats 50 people pasting into the consumer free tier.

title: Publish an approved-tools list
body: A short, opinionated list of which AI tools are sanctioned for which use cases. Update quarterly.

title: Set up an internal API gateway for LLM calls
body: Route all model calls through one gateway so you can log, rate-limit, swap models, and track cost per team.

title: Build a shared prompt and pattern library
body: Curated, version-controlled prompts and agent patterns the whole org can reuse. Compounds value across teams.

title: Map the top 3 workflows where AI could remove drudgery
body: Pick workflows you actually own and watch where humans copy-paste between systems. That is your AI roadmap.

title: Embed AI into one daily workflow end-to-end
body: Not a side tool. Built into the system of record people already use. One workflow done well beats five pilots.

title: Instrument the workflow with before/after metrics
body: Cycle time, error rate, throughput. Without measurement you cannot defend the budget.

title: Refactor the surrounding process around the AI step
body: Most value is unlocked when you redesign the workflow around the AI capability, not bolt it on.

title: Run a mandatory 60-minute AI literacy session
body: Every employee, same baseline. What LLMs are, what they are not, where the org draws lines.

title: Identify and resource a champions network
body: Find the 5-10% who are already power users. Give them time, recognition, and a Slack channel.

title: Run role-specific prompting workshops
body: Generic training underwhelms. A 2-hour session for sales, for finance, for engineering — each with their own examples — lands.

title: Add AI fluency to performance and hiring criteria
body: You get the behaviour you measure. Make this part of how people are evaluated and hired.

title: Publish an acceptable-use policy for AI
body: One page. What is allowed, what is not, what to do when unsure. Mandatory acknowledgement.

title: Define a use-case intake and risk triage
body: A lightweight form + 3-tier risk rating (low/medium/high) so teams know when they need a deeper review.

title: Stand up an AI review committee
body: Cross-functional (legal, security, data, business). Meets every two weeks. Approves medium/high risk use cases.

title: Implement model and prompt logging for audit
body: Capture what was sent, what came back, who approved it. Non-negotiable for regulated industries; valuable for everyone.

title: Pick one KPI per active AI bet
body: Cycle time, conversion, NPS, cost-per-ticket. One number. If you cannot pick one, you do not have a use case.

title: Establish baselines before rolling out
body: Measure the world without AI for 2-4 weeks. Without a baseline, every claim of impact is anecdote.

title: Run quarterly value reviews on each initiative
body: Force every initiative to defend itself every 90 days. Kill the bottom third. Reinvest.

title: Build a single AI value dashboard
body: One view: spend, adoption, KPI movement, top wins. Shared with the leadership team monthly.

title: Have leaders use AI visibly in their own work
body: Nothing accelerates adoption like the CEO showing the prompt they used in the last all-hands.

title: Create a no-blame channel for AI experiments
body: A Slack/Teams channel where people share what they tried — wins and flops. Normalizes learning in public.

title: Celebrate and amplify three internal wins per quarter
body: Real stories, real names, real numbers. Beats any external case study for changing minds internally.

title: Reframe AI in roles as augmentation, not replacement
body: Communicate a clear stance from leadership about how roles evolve. Ambiguity is the killer of adoption.

title: Decide your stance on AI in screening, in writing, this quarter
body: Write a one-page stance on AI in screening, get exec sign-off.
why_matters: AI in screening is a regulatory and reputational risk in 2026. Most People functions have no written stance, which means individual recruiters are making the call.
what_to_do: Draft a one-page position: where AI is used in screening, where it is not, what gets logged. Get exec sign-off. Brief the team.
how_to_know: Every recruiter can articulate the stance without checking a doc.

title: Pilot Claude Cowork for one People process
body: Pilot Claude Cowork on your onboarding workflow.
why_matters: Claude Cowork file and task automation is well-suited to People processes (onboarding checklists, joiner packs, leaver workflows). This is a low-stakes way to evaluate the tool against a real People use case.
what_to_do: Pick one process (onboarding is usually best). Use Cowork to automate the file prep, scheduling coordination, and follow-up tasks for the next 5 joiners. Compare time and error rate to before.
how_to_know: Onboarding admin time drops by at least 50% across the 5 joiners.

title: Appoint an AI exec sponsor with budget authority
body: Name an AI exec sponsor with budget authority and a quarterly cadence with the CEO.
why_matters: Your organisation is past the point where AI can be left to enthusiasts. Without a named exec with budget authority and a quarterly review cadence, every other Move on this list will stall.
what_to_do: At your next leadership meeting, name the sponsor. Define the remit in three lines: portfolio of bets, budget envelope, quarterly review with the CEO. Tell the company.
how_to_know: Within four weeks, the sponsor has approved or rejected at least three AI investment proposals using a stated framework.

title: Stand up an AI governance one-pager, not a committee
body: Replace your AI governance committee with a one-pager that names the rules.
why_matters: Most companies your size build governance committees that slow everything down. A one-pager that names the rules and the escalation path beats a committee.
what_to_do: Draft a single page covering: sanctioned tools, sensitive-data rules, where humans must review, who decides on new tools, how incidents get reported. Publish it. Iterate every quarter.
how_to_know: Every senior leader can name the three rules that matter most. The doc has been edited at least once in the last quarter.

title: Run an AI fluency pulse across your top 3 functions
body: Run a 10-question fluency pulse across your top 3 functions.
why_matters: You do not know where your real fluency gaps are. Self-assessment by exec is wrong in both directions. A short, anonymous pulse across the top 3 functions tells you where to invest.
what_to_do: 10-question survey to RevOps, Marketing, and one operations-heavy function. Report results back to the exec sponsor. Use it to size the next training investment.
how_to_know: You can name the function with the biggest fluency gap and the gap shape (tooling, prompting, workflow, or trust).

title: Rebuild one cross-company workflow this quarter
body: Rebuild one cross-company workflow as the new default this quarter.
why_matters: Function-by-function AI work plateaus around Tier 3. The next jump comes from rebuilding a workflow that crosses two or more functions.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow that touches two functions. Map it. Identify which steps an agent can do, which a human must. Rebuild it as the new default this quarter.
how_to_know: At quarter-end, the workflow is the new default for at least 50% of instances. Cycle time has measurably dropped.

title: Make AI investment a standing P&L line by Q3
body: Consolidate AI spend into a single P&L line by Q3.
why_matters: AI spend is currently scattered across IT, People, and individual function budgets. Until it is a line on the exec dashboard, ROI conversations stay anecdotal.
what_to_do: Work with Finance to consolidate AI tooling, infrastructure, and capability spend into a single P&L line for Q3 onwards. Add an "outcomes per pound" view for the sponsor quarterly review.
how_to_know: At the Q3 review, the sponsor presents AI investment as a single number with a stated outcome target.

title: Brief the board, in writing, by next board meeting
body: Send a one-page AI briefing to the board 5 days before the next meeting.
why_matters: Board awareness lags operational reality at your size. A short, honest written briefing changes the kind of question they ask and unlocks the next round of investment.
what_to_do: One-page brief: where AI is operating today, where it is about to be, the three biggest risks, the ask. Send 5 days before the next board meeting.
how_to_know: At the meeting, the AI conversation is led by data the board has already seen. No surprises.

title: Name one person whose job is AI, this month
body: Name an interim AI lead with a 90-day mandate to ship one workflow.
why_matters: Without a named owner, nothing moves. Strategy decks do not ship workflows.
what_to_do: At the next leadership meeting, name an interim AI lead. 25% of their time, mandate to ship one workflow end-to-end in 90 days. Tell the company.
how_to_know: In 90 days, one workflow is in production and the lead can name what blocked it.

title: Inventory the data that actually exists, not the data you wish you had
body: Inventory the data that actually exists in one function and publish the map.
why_matters: Most orgs at this tier overestimate their data foundations. A two-week inventory tells you where the real starting line is.
what_to_do: Pick one function. List the data sources, who owns them, and what state they are actually in. Be honest about gaps. Publish the map internally.
how_to_know: You can answer "where would an AI agent get its inputs from for this function" in one sentence.

title: Ship one workflow end-to-end before any strategy doc
body: Ship one rebuilt workflow end-to-end in 60 days with no committees.
why_matters: Strategy docs without shipped workflows are theatre. Pick one and ship it.
what_to_do: Pick the highest-debt workflow in any function. Give the AI lead 60 days to rebuild it with AI as the spine. No committees. Report at quarter-end.
how_to_know: In 60 days, the rebuilt workflow is the new default for at least 50% of instances.

title: Get five execs onto Claude or ChatGPT Teams this month
body: Get the top 5 execs onto a sanctioned AI tool with one onboarding session.
why_matters: You cannot govern what you do not use. Exec fluency is the unblock for everything downstream.
what_to_do: Provision Claude or ChatGPT Teams seats for the top 5 execs. Give them one onboarding session. Set an expectation that AI is in their workflow within a fortnight.
how_to_know: Within a month, every exec can describe one task they have moved to AI.

title: Publish the three rules everyone needs, no committee
body: Publish three governance rules on a one-pager, revisit in 90 days.
why_matters: At low tiers, the risk is paralysis through governance. A one-pager with three rules beats a quarterly meeting.
what_to_do: Write three rules: what data never goes into AI, what tools are sanctioned, who decides on new tools. Publish. Revisit in 90 days.
how_to_know: Every senior leader can recite the three rules without checking the doc.

title: Stand up an evals and observability spine
body: Stand up an evals and observability spine before the next wave of agents.
why_matters: At your tier, the next failure mode is silent regression. You need evals at scale and observability before the next wave of agents.
what_to_do: Pick a platform (Braintrust, LangSmith, Humanloop, or roll-your-own). Migrate evals from your top 3 agents onto it. Wire alerts on regression. Make it a standing review.
how_to_know: You can show a regression on an agent within 24 hours of it appearing, not 24 days.

title: Re-cut one function around the model, not alongside it
body: Re-cut one function around the model and promote an agent operator role.
why_matters: At this tier, the next leap is org-design, not more tools. Pick one function and bend the structure around the model.
what_to_do: Pick the function with the most agent leverage today. Redesign the org chart on a single page. Re-cut JDs. Promote one role to "agent operator". Brief the function in person.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, the function performance metrics show step-change, not incremental gains.

title: Pick one content type and rebuild it with AI as the spine
body: Rebuild your highest-volume content type with AI as the spine.
why_matters: Marketing functions at this tier scatter AI across many tasks. The leverage comes from going deep on one.
what_to_do: Pick the content type with the highest volume (blog, social, email). Rebuild the workflow with Claude as the drafter, your style guide as instruction, and a human review at the end.
how_to_know: Within 6 weeks, that content type ships in half the time at equal or better quality.

title: Codify your brand voice in a Claude Project
body: Codify your brand voice in a Claude Project so output stays on-brand.
why_matters: Brand voice drift is the #1 reason marketing teams stop trusting AI output. Codify it once, ship it everywhere.
what_to_do: Build a Claude Project with your top 10 best-on-brand pieces, your tone-of-voice doc, and your three "never" rules. Test on five new pieces. Iterate.
how_to_know: A new starter can produce on-brand copy from the Project on day one.

title: Stop A/B testing without an AI variant
body: Add an AI-drafted variant to every A/B test for the next quarter.
why_matters: Every test should include an AI-drafted variant. If yours do not, you are leaving the data on the table.
what_to_do: For the next 5 tests, add one AI-drafted variant to the mix. Track win rate against human-drafted.
how_to_know: You have data on whether AI variants beat human variants in your context.

title: Move every engineer onto Claude Code or Cursor this month
body: Move every engineer onto a code agent this month.
why_matters: Code agents are the highest-leverage AI move available to engineering. The cost of waiting is now bigger than the cost of switching.
what_to_do: Provision Claude Code or Cursor seats for every IC. One-hour onboarding. Set the expectation that PRs use it.
how_to_know: Within a month, 80% of PRs have AI-assisted authorship.

title: Ship one internal Skill / agent for code review
body: Ship a code-review agent that handles your 5 most common review comments.
why_matters: Code review is repetitive, leveraged, and sits in the path of every change. A team-tuned reviewer agent compounds.
what_to_do: Pick the 5 most common review comments in your team. Encode them as a Claude Skill or GitHub Action that runs on every PR. Review the output for two weeks, then trust it.
how_to_know: The team accepts 80%+ of the agent comments without amendment.

title: Add evals to one production AI feature this quarter
body: Add 30 evals to your highest-impact AI feature and block release on regression.
why_matters: Evals are the difference between shipping AI features and shipping AI demos. One feature is enough to start.
what_to_do: Pick the AI feature with the most user impact. Write 30 evals covering the happy path and 5 known failure modes. Run on every deploy. Block release on regression.
how_to_know: You can name the eval that would catch any production regression in this feature.

title: Write your one-page personal AI mandate
body: Personal mandate: one page, twelve weeks, three handoff tasks.
why_matters: Without a stated personal stance, your AI use stays reactive. A one-pager makes the next twelve weeks deliberate.
what_to_do: Spend 30 minutes drafting a single page: what role you want AI to play in your week, three tasks you will hand off first, two you will keep human, one outcome you want by the end of the quarter. Keep it on your desktop.
how_to_know: In two weeks, you can name the three tasks you have moved to AI without checking the doc.

title: Pick a quarterly AI bet and tell two people
body: Quarterly bet, named witnesses, dated review.
why_matters: You are using AI well already. The next move is to commit publicly to one bet so it gets prioritised over background tasks.
what_to_do: Choose one outcome for the next 90 days that AI is the primary lever for. Tell two colleagues what it is and what success looks like. Put a date in the calendar to review it.
how_to_know: At the 90-day review you can show evidence of the bet either landing or being killed with a clear reason.

title: Sponsor someone else through the same shift
body: Sponsor three peers, fortnightly, for one quarter.
why_matters: At your level the leverage is no longer your own use. It is making three other people operate the way you do.
what_to_do: Pick three colleagues who are at the level you were six months ago. Give each 30 minutes a fortnight. Bring one move you made; have them try it before the next session.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, at least two of the three are using a Claude Project or agent without you in the loop.

title: Tidy the inputs you give AI, this week
body: Canonical inputs folder. Three files. Used by reflex.
why_matters: Most personal AI output is mediocre because the input is messy. Cleaner sources, cleaner answers.
what_to_do: Pick the three documents you paste into AI most often (a CV, a pitch deck, a product brief, your team handbook). Save clean canonical versions in one folder. Reference that folder every time.
how_to_know: By Friday, you reach for the canonical folder by reflex when starting a new prompt.

title: Build a personal evidence library inside Claude
body: Personal evidence Project, weekly use.
why_matters: You give AI good inputs already. The next gain is making your evidence reusable across every prompt.
what_to_do: In Claude, create a Project called "My evidence". Add: your three best work samples, your CV, your last 5 client briefs, anything you reference repeatedly. Use it as the home for any task that needs you-specific context.
how_to_know: Within a fortnight you stop re-pasting your background into prompts.

title: Connect one MCP source to your daily AI surface
body: One live MCP source. One workflow rebuilt.
why_matters: You are past the point where copy-paste is the bottleneck. The next horizon is having AI read live state, not snapshots.
what_to_do: Pick one source that holds your work context (Linear, Notion, Gmail, Drive). Set up an MCP connection or the equivalent native integration so Claude or your assistant of choice can read it directly. Use it for one workflow this week.
how_to_know: You complete a task you used to do manually without copy-pasting any source content.

title: Pick one assistant and stop tab-switching
body: Pick one. Pin it. Two weeks. Decide.
why_matters: Switching between three chat windows is its own tax. Pick one and use it for everything for two weeks.
what_to_do: Choose Claude or ChatGPT. Pin it. Use it for every AI task for the next fortnight. At the end, decide whether the second tool earns its place back.
how_to_know: After two weeks you can name a specific task where the unused tool would have done it better. Or you cannot, and you delete it.

title: Move from chat to Projects and Skills
body: Three Projects or Skills, daily use.
why_matters: Chat is fine for one-off tasks. The compounding only starts when you build durable surfaces.
what_to_do: List the three tasks you do with AI most often. For each, build a Claude Project (with instructions and reference docs) or a Skill. Use them this week. Refine the instructions once.
how_to_know: By the end of the week you reach for a Project or Skill at least daily.

title: Stand up a personal automation in n8n or Zapier
body: One personal automation. Ten executions. Two weeks.
why_matters: Your tooling is solid. The leverage now is letting work happen without you starting it.
what_to_do: Pick one recurring trigger you handle manually (an inbound email type, a calendar event, a form submission). Build a small n8n or Zapier flow that calls Claude and either drafts the response or files the artefact. Run it for two weeks.
how_to_know: After two weeks the flow has fired at least 10 times and you have approved the output without major edits.

title: Make AI the first draft for one weekly task
body: One task. AI first draft. No exceptions. Two weeks.
why_matters: Most people use AI on the side. The shift comes when one specific task always starts with AI.
what_to_do: Pick one weekly task that involves writing or analysis. From this week, the rule is: never start it without AI generating the first draft. No exceptions for two weeks.
how_to_know: After two weeks you have a clear view on whether AI cuts the time meaningfully or whether the task does not suit it.

title: Rebuild your weekly review around AI
body: AI in the weekly review. Three prompts. One month.
why_matters: Your AI use is solid in pockets. Your weekly review is where it should be braided into how you operate, not bolted on.
what_to_do: In your weekly review, add three steps: ask AI to summarise what you wrote and decided this week, ask it to flag anything that contradicts last week, ask it for the one thing you should drop. Do this for a month.
how_to_know: After a month you can name two changes to your week that came out of these reviews.

title: Run one workflow without you in the loop
body: One workflow. No human-in-the-loop start. Three weeks.
why_matters: You have integrated AI into how you work. The next move is to remove yourself from one step entirely.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow where you are currently the bottleneck (triage, scheduling, response drafting). Build it as an agent or automation that runs without you starting it. Review the output weekly, not in real time.
how_to_know: After three weeks the workflow has run at least 15 times and you have intervened in fewer than 3.

title: Move off your personal ChatGPT account this week
body: Sanctioned account, all work prompts, by Friday.
why_matters: Personal accounts and work data are an unforced error. The fix is small.
what_to_do: Check whether your company has a sanctioned Claude or ChatGPT Teams account. If yes, move all work prompts there this week. If no, ask once, in writing, who owns it.
how_to_know: By Friday you can show your last 10 work prompts on the sanctioned account.

title: Write your personal redaction rules
body: Personal redaction card. Always-on.
why_matters: You handle sensitive inputs already. A two-line rule beats a vibe.
what_to_do: Write down on one card the things you will never paste into AI (client names, salary data, M&A material, HR records). Stick it next to your screen. Apply it.
how_to_know: You can recite the rules without checking the card.

title: Add a citation check to your AI workflow
body: Citation check, default in the workflow.
why_matters: You ship AI-assisted output that other people rely on. Verifiable sources is the next bar.
what_to_do: For any output you publish or send externally, add a step where AI cites its sources and you check at least two of them. Build it into a Skill or saved prompt so the check is the default.
how_to_know: Within a fortnight you have caught at least one factual error before it shipped.

title: Track time saved on one task for two weeks
body: One task. Ten data points. Two weeks.
why_matters: Without a number, AI is a feeling. With one, it is a case for more time.
what_to_do: Pick one task. For the next two weeks, log start and end time when you do it with AI and when you do it without. Aim for 5 of each.
how_to_know: You can produce a before/after number you would defend in a 1:1.

title: Keep a personal AI changelog
body: Weekly changelog, three lines, one month.
why_matters: You make moves every week and forget them by the next quarter. A changelog turns activity into a story.
what_to_do: Open a single document. Each Friday, log: what you tried this week, what worked, what you killed. Three lines max each.
how_to_know: After a month you can hand the changelog to your manager as your AI work narrative.

title: Quantify one workflow you rebuilt
body: One workflow, one page, named recipient.
why_matters: You have rebuilt workflows already. Show the number so the company invests in the next one.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow you have AI-assisted. Measure: time per instance before and after, error rate before and after, your own intervention rate. Write it up on one page. Send to your sponsor.
how_to_know: Your sponsor cites the number in their next leadership update.

title: Show one AI move in your next team meeting
body: Five-minute demo, monthly cadence.
why_matters: Quiet AI use does not change the team. Visible use does.
what_to_do: In your next team meeting, demo one thing AI helped you do this week. Five minutes max. Do not pitch the tool; show the work.
how_to_know: Within two meetings, someone else demos something back.

title: Run a 30-minute monthly clinic for your team
body: Monthly 30-minute clinic. One task type per session.
why_matters: Knowledge sticks when it gets practiced. A monthly clinic is the smallest forum that produces compounding.
what_to_do: Block 30 minutes a month. Pick one task type. Bring two prompts. Have everyone try them on their own work. Compare outputs.
how_to_know: After three clinics, two teammates have built a Project or Skill of their own.

title: Write one teardown a quarter and publish it
body: Quarterly teardown, 800 words, one published.
why_matters: You operate ahead of the curve. Writing the teardown is what makes the curve move.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow you rebuilt. Write 800 words: what it was, what you did, what worked, what did not, what you would do next. Publish internally or externally.
how_to_know: The piece gets shared by at least one peer outside your team within two weeks.

title: Stand up a federated data product layer for AI
body: Three data products. Contracts. Quarterly review.
why_matters: At your maturity, the gating issue is not data quality on any one domain. It is consistent access across domains for agents.
what_to_do: Pick the three domains agents need to read across (customer, product usage, finance). Assign a product owner per domain. Publish a clear contract: schema, refresh, SLA, sensitivity. Make agents consume only the contract, not the underlying systems.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, every agent in production reads from a contract, not a raw table.

title: Consolidate to two model providers and an internal gateway
body: Two providers. One gateway. Cost per FTE down.
why_matters: Tool sprawl is the operating cost of last quarter's adoption push. Consolidation is what makes the next quarter cheaper.
what_to_do: Audit every paid AI tool. Pick two model providers (typically Anthropic and OpenAI). Stand up an internal gateway so every team consumes models through one URL with logging, rate limits and cost attribution. Retire the rest.
how_to_know: Quarterly AI spend per FTE drops while usage rises.

title: Pick one cross-functional workflow and rebuild it as agents
body: One cross-function workflow. New default. Quarter horizon.
why_matters: Single-function AI work plateaus. The next jump is a workflow that crosses two or three functions and is owned end to end.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow that crosses functions (lead-to-close, hire-to-onboard, incident-to-postmortem). Map current state. Identify which steps an agent owns, which a human reviews, which a human owns. Ship the new default this quarter.
how_to_know: At quarter end, the new flow is the default for at least 50% of instances. Cycle time has measurably dropped.

title: Promote a Function AI Owner in every priority function
body: Five Function AI Owners. 20% time. Quarterly review.
why_matters: You have fluency. You do not have ownership. Function AI Owners are how fluency turns into shipped systems.
what_to_do: Name a Function AI Owner in each of the top 5 functions. Carve 20% of their week. Their job: ship and maintain agents and Skills used by their function. Quarterly review with the exec sponsor.
how_to_know: Every Owner has shipped at least one agent or Skill in active use within a quarter.

title: Publish an AI value scorecard the exec team reviews monthly
body: Monthly scorecard. 5–8 metrics. Exec review.
why_matters: Anecdote-driven AI conversations stop being persuasive at your size. A scorecard moves the conversation from belief to evidence.
what_to_do: Define 5–8 outcome metrics across cost, cycle time, quality, and adoption. Wire them to source systems. Publish monthly. Review at the exec meeting. Kill any bet whose metrics have not moved in two quarters.
how_to_know: The exec team can name the three metrics that moved last month and the bet attached to each.

title: Make AI-native ways of working the default in hiring
body: Hiring updates. Fluency interview. Onboarding parity.
why_matters: Your existing team has shifted. New joiners revert to old patterns unless hiring and onboarding bake in the new defaults.
what_to_do: Update every job description in the priority functions to name the AI tools and ways of working expected. Add a 30-minute AI-fluency segment to interviews for relevant roles. Onboard new joiners onto the same Projects and Skills veterans use.
how_to_know: New joiners reach productivity on AI-assisted workflows in their first month.

title: Run a quarterly AI risk review with named owners
body: Quarterly risk review. One-page summary. Named owners.
why_matters: At your scale, AI risk lives in too many places to govern by policy alone. A standing review is what keeps it visible.
what_to_do: Stand up a 60-minute quarterly review with the exec sponsor, Legal, Security, and the top 3 function owners. Agenda: incidents, near-misses, new tools, policy changes, audit log spot-check. Publish a one-page summary.
how_to_know: Every senior leader has seen the last quarterly summary and can name the top risk.

title: Write a one-page RevOps AI thesis this fortnight
body: One-page thesis. Two priorities. CRO sign-off.
why_matters: Without a stated thesis, every RevOps AI conversation re-litigates the same five questions. A page settles them.
what_to_do: On one page name: which two parts of the funnel AI rebuilds first, what stays human, what tools you sanction, who owns it, what success looks like in 90 days. Get your VP Sales and the CRO to mark it up. Ship v2 the next week.
how_to_know: Within two weeks every Sales manager can recite the two AI priorities for the funnel.

title: Tie every active RevOps AI bet to a pipeline metric
body: Pipeline metric per bet. Ruthless cull.
why_matters: You have multiple bets running. Without a metric per bet, sponsorship stays soft.
what_to_do: List every AI bet RevOps owns. For each, name the pipeline metric it should move (cycle time, win rate, meetings booked, qualified leads per AE). If a bet has no clear metric, kill it or rewrite it.
how_to_know: In your next pipeline review the AI bets are discussed using the same metrics as everything else.

title: Restructure RevOps around the agent stack you actually run
body: New org chart. Agent owners. Comp realigned.
why_matters: Your team is still shaped around manual workflows. The org chart is now the bottleneck, not the tooling.
what_to_do: Map the agent stack you have. Re-cut the team: who owns each agent, who owns evals, who owns the human-in-the-loop reviews. Publish the new org. Adjust comp lines accordingly.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, every named agent has a single owner and a measurable SLA.

title: Fix the top 5 fields in your CRM before adding any agent
body: Five fields. 90% completeness. Validation rules.
why_matters: Agents trained on dirty CRM data are louder versions of bad data. Cleanup is the unglamorous prerequisite.
what_to_do: Pick the 5 CRM fields agents will read or write (account, stage, next step, ICP fit, owner). Audit completeness on the last 90 days. Set a one-week cleanup sprint with named owners. Add validation rules so the rot does not return.
how_to_know: Field completeness on those 5 fields hits 90%+ within two weeks.

title: Pipe Gong (or your call recorder) into your AI surface
body: Gong piped. AE-level summaries. Pipeline review.
why_matters: Call recordings are the highest-value Sales context you have and the least connected to your AI tools.
what_to_do: Set up the Gong (or Chorus, Fathom) integration into Claude or your sanctioned assistant. Pilot one use case: have AI summarise the last 5 calls per AE before each pipeline review.
how_to_know: AEs reference call summaries unprompted in the next pipeline review.

title: Build a Sales evidence layer agents read across CRM, calls, and tickets
body: Evidence layer. One agent. Quality A/B.
why_matters: Your agents are reading from individual silos. Multi-source context is what turns a useful agent into a great one.
what_to_do: Stand up an evidence layer (Snowflake, BigQuery, or a vector store) that pulls from CRM, call recordings and support tickets nightly. Build one agent that reads from it for account research. Compare quality to the single-source baseline.
how_to_know: The multi-source agent produces account briefs your AEs prefer over the existing single-source brief.

title: Sanction one AI assistant for Sales and turn off the rest
body: One sanctioned tool. Onboarded. Audited.
why_matters: Sales reps using personal ChatGPT for prospect data is your top governance risk. Pick a sanctioned tool, fast.
what_to_do: Buy Claude Teams or ChatGPT Teams (whichever your stack supports). Onboard every AE in one 30-minute session. Publish the rule: this is the only sanctioned account for prospect or customer data.
how_to_know: Within two weeks every AE can show their last 10 prompts on the sanctioned account.

title: Adopt the AI features inside the Sales tools you already pay for
body: Vertical AI map. Owners. Quarterly review.
why_matters: Salesforce Einstein, HubSpot Breeze, Gong AI, Outreach AI, Clay — they are sitting in your stack already. Most teams use 10% of them.
what_to_do: For each Sales tool you pay for, list the AI features. Mark which are on, which are off, which the team uses. Turn on the highest-leverage ones this quarter (call coaching, email AI, forecast AI). Disable anything sensitive that is not sanctioned.
how_to_know: You can produce a one-page AI-in-Sales tooling map with named owners.

title: Move agent orchestration off vendor tools onto your own n8n
body: Three agents. Parity test. Migration.
why_matters: Vendor agent builders are fine until you need to compose them. n8n (or LangGraph) is the lowest-effort way to take ownership.
what_to_do: Pick your three highest-value Sales agents. Rebuild them in n8n with Claude as the model. Keep the vendor versions running for two weeks for parity testing. Cut over.
how_to_know: After two weeks the n8n versions match or beat vendor output and cost less to run.

title: Run a 60-minute Sales AI baseline session this month
body: One session. Three prompts. Live practice.
why_matters: AEs are using AI without a shared baseline. One session removes 80% of the bad habits.
what_to_do: Block 60 minutes for the whole AE team. Show: the sanctioned tool, three useful prompts (account research, follow-up email, objection handling), the rules on what not to paste. Have everyone try them on a real account live.
how_to_know: In the next pipeline review, two AEs reference one of the three prompts unprompted.

title: Build a shared Sales prompt library inside Claude Projects
body: Workflow Projects. Shared. Tracked use.
why_matters: Each AE prompting from scratch is the second-biggest waste in the function. A shared library with versioning is the fix.
what_to_do: Create a Claude Project per AE workflow (account research, proposal, follow-up, objection handling). Add the best 3 prompts and reference docs to each. Make every AE use them this quarter. Track which Projects get used.
how_to_know: Three Projects show daily use across the team within a month.

title: Make AI proficiency a standard part of AE ramp and review
body: Onboarding block. Quarterly review question. AE OKR.
why_matters: Your top AEs use AI well. The middle of the bell curve does not. Built-in expectation closes the gap.
what_to_do: Add an AI-fluency block to onboarding (the first month covers the sanctioned tools, the shared Projects, and three workflows). Add a question on AI use to every quarterly review. Tie one OKR per AE to AI-assisted output.
how_to_know: New AEs hit ramp targets faster than their predecessor cohort.

title: Make pipeline review an agent-prepared meeting
body: Pre-read agent. Per account. Four-week test.
why_matters: Pipeline review is the highest-value recurring meeting in RevOps and the most under-prepared.
what_to_do: Build an agent that reads CRM, call summaries and email activity, and produces a one-page brief per account in slip risk before every pipeline review. Send 24 hours ahead. Run for 4 weeks.
how_to_know: Pipeline review time drops by 30% and fewer accounts get rolled.

title: Shift CRM hygiene from human nag to agent fix
body: Hygiene agent. Daily approval flow.
why_matters: Manual CRM hygiene is the worst use of AE time. An agent that proposes the fix and asks for approval is the right shape.
what_to_do: Build an agent that scans CRM nightly for the 5 fields you care about, drafts the fix from call notes and emails, and sends a one-click approval to the AE each morning.
how_to_know: Field completeness stays above 90% with under 10 minutes per AE per day.

title: Publish three rules for AI in Sales, on one page
body: Three rules. One brief. Memorised.
why_matters: Sales is the function most likely to misuse AI on customer data. A long policy gets ignored. Three rules do not.
what_to_do: Write three rules: where to use AI (sanctioned tool only), what never to paste (full prospect lists, contract terms), what gets logged (anything with named accounts). Publish to the team. Brief once.
how_to_know: Every AE can recite the three rules without looking them up.

title: Log every Sales agent prompt and review monthly
body: Prompt log. Monthly spot-check. Trend down.
why_matters: Logging is what turns governance from a vibe into evidence.
what_to_do: Pipe the sanctioned tool's prompt logs into a single dashboard. Each month spot-check 50 random prompts. Flag anything that breaks the rules. Brief the team on patterns.
how_to_know: In the second month, prompt-rule violations drop 80% from baseline.

title: Stand up evals on every customer-facing Sales agent
body: Evals per customer-facing agent. Weekly run. Deploy gate.
why_matters: Customer-facing agents without evals are a pricing or compliance incident waiting to happen.
what_to_do: For every agent that touches customer data or output (call summarisers, email drafts, proposal generators), define an eval set. Run weekly. Block deploys that drop a key metric.
how_to_know: In the first quarter, at least one regression is caught by evals before it ships.

title: Pick one funnel metric and instrument it before any AI bet
body: One metric. 90-day baseline. Re-measure.
why_matters: AI wins in Sales without a baseline are stories. With a baseline they are budget.
what_to_do: Choose one funnel metric (lead-to-meeting time, meeting-to-opp rate, opp cycle time). Measure the last 90 days. Then run any AI move. Re-measure.
how_to_know: You can show a before/after on one metric the CRO will quote.

title: Build a Sales AI scorecard updated weekly
body: Weekly scorecard. AE all-hands. Exec citation.
why_matters: You have multiple AI bets. A scorecard is the only way the CRO sees them as a portfolio, not anecdotes.
what_to_do: Build a single dashboard with: time saved per AE, AI-assisted pipeline, win rate on AI-assisted opps vs control. Update weekly. Review at the AE all-hands.
how_to_know: The CRO references the scorecard in their next exec update.

title: Publish AI-assisted vs unassisted win rates by AE
body: AI-attributed win rate. Per AE. Coaching input.
why_matters: You have enough volume to make this analysis honest. The transparency itself drives adoption.
what_to_do: For the last two quarters, segment opps by whether the AE used the sanctioned AI tools (logged), and report win rates and cycle times by AE. Share with the team. Coach from it.
how_to_know: AEs in the bottom quartile of AI use either move up or are reassigned within a quarter.

title: Open a #sales-ai-wins channel and seed it with three of your own
body: Channel. Three seeds. Tagged AEs. Four-week hold.
why_matters: AEs copy what they see. A channel where wins are visible is the cheapest culture lever you have.
what_to_do: Open #sales-ai-wins on Slack. Post three of your own wins from this week to seed it. Tag two AEs to share theirs by Friday. Hold the cadence for four weeks.
how_to_know: After four weeks the channel has at least 20 posts and you are no longer the top poster.

title: Make the best AE the visible owner of one Sales agent
body: Top AE owns one agent. Monthly demo.
why_matters: The strongest signal you can send is that an AE you respect runs an agent. Stops the "AI is something Ops does" framing.
what_to_do: Pick your top AE. Give them ownership of one agent (likely the call summariser or pre-call brief). Have them present it monthly to the team.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, two more AEs have asked to own an agent.

title: Tie individual AE comp accelerator to AI-assisted productivity
body: Comp accelerator. One pod. One quarter.
why_matters: Comp is the hardest culture lever and the most powerful. Used carefully, it locks in behaviour for years.
what_to_do: Work with Finance and the CRO to add a small accelerator (5–10% of variable) tied to AI-assisted pipeline or AI-assisted productivity metrics. Pilot with a single AE pod for a quarter. Iterate.
how_to_know: After one quarter the pod outperforms control on the targeted metric and AEs ask for it to expand.

title: Pick three content types AI rebuilds first
body: Three content types. AI spine. 90 days.
why_matters: A team that tries to AI everything ends up AIing nothing well. Three named types is the right scope.
what_to_do: Choose three (case study, blog post, email nurture, sales enablement deck, social post). Commit that every instance of those three uses AI as the spine for the next 90 days. Leave the rest alone.
how_to_know: Within six weeks the three types are produced 50% faster and your team can name what changed.

title: Move from content team to content system this quarter
body: Pipeline map. Owners. SLA. One campaign.
why_matters: You are producing more with AI but still organised by hands not by pipeline. The next jump is structural.
what_to_do: Map your content production as a pipeline (research → outline → draft → edit → approve → publish → repurpose). For each step, name the AI tool, the human owner, and the SLA. Publish the pipeline. Run one campaign through it.
how_to_know: One campaign moves through the pipeline in half the time of the previous baseline.

title: Define a brand position on AI in marketing, in writing
body: Public AI brand position. One page. Linked publicly.
why_matters: Your competitors will use AI badly. Naming the difference, in public, is itself a marketing move.
what_to_do: Write a one-page public position on how your team uses AI: what it does, what humans always do, what gets disclosed. Publish it. Reference it in every relevant pitch.
how_to_know: Within a quarter the position is referenced by at least one customer or analyst.

title: Build the canonical brand voice doc and put it in Claude
body: Brand voice doc. In a Project. Used by reflex.
why_matters: Most AI-written marketing sounds the same. Your brand voice doc, put in front of every prompt, is the cheapest fix.
what_to_do: Write or update a 2-page brand voice doc: 5 dos, 5 do nots, 3 example sentences each. Add it as the reference doc in a Claude Project. Make every drafting task use it.
how_to_know: Within a fortnight, the difference between AI-written and human-written copy is hard to spot.

title: Pull your top 50 historical assets into a marketing evidence Project
body: Top 50 in a Project. Default seed for new work.
why_matters: Generic AI marketing is the result of generic context. Your own best work is the best context you have.
what_to_do: Pick your 50 best-performing assets across the last two years (blog, case studies, decks, emails). Add them to a Claude Project as references. Use it as the seed for every new asset.
how_to_know: New assets show measurable lift in engagement vs the control set within a quarter.

title: Connect product analytics to your AI marketing surface
body: Analytics piped. Behavioural campaign. A/B win.
why_matters: Brand and craft only get you so far. Once analytics is wired in, AI can write campaigns about behaviours not personas.
what_to_do: Pipe product analytics (Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog) into your AI surface via MCP or a dedicated dataset. Build one campaign that targets a specific behaviour cohort.
how_to_know: The behaviour-targeted campaign outperforms the persona-targeted control on the headline metric.

title: Sanction one writing assistant and turn off the rest
body: One tool. Onboarded. Rest cancelled.
why_matters: Marketing teams accumulate tools faster than any other function. Pick one and the team gets faster, not slower.
what_to_do: Choose Claude (preferred for craft) or ChatGPT Teams. Onboard the team in one session. Cancel the rest at the next renewal.
how_to_know: Within a month the team uses one tool by default and rates it as their primary surface.

title: Audit AI features inside the marketing stack you already pay for
body: Vertical AI map. Owners. Quarterly review.
why_matters: HubSpot Breeze, Marketo Einstein, Adobe Firefly, Mailchimp Intuit Assist — most of the AI you need is already in your stack.
what_to_do: List every paid marketing tool. For each, find what AI it ships and what is enabled. Switch on the highest-leverage features (subject lines, segmentation, asset generation). Disable anything that touches PII without sanction.
how_to_know: You can produce a one-page vertical-AI map for marketing with named owners.

title: Stand up a marketing-owned automation surface in n8n
body: Three n8n flows. Marketer-owned. Engineering unblocked.
why_matters: Marketing ops shouldn't be blocked on engineering for every workflow. n8n with Claude is the right ownership boundary.
what_to_do: Pick your three highest-volume marketing workflows (lead enrichment, asset repurposing, campaign reporting). Build them in n8n. Have one marketer own the surface.
how_to_know: Within a quarter the three workflows run unattended and your engineering team has no marketing tickets.

title: Make the brief-to-draft cycle 24 hours, with AI
body: Brief template. 24-hour SLA. Voice Project.
why_matters: The slowest part of marketing is brief to first draft. AI collapses it without losing voice if the brief is sharp.
what_to_do: Standardise a one-page brief template (audience, job-to-be-done, key proof, tone, length). Rule: every brief returns a first draft from AI within 24 hours, using the brand voice Project.
how_to_know: Within a fortnight, time from brief to first draft drops to under 24 hours on every asset.

title: Build a repurposing pipeline for every long-form asset
body: Five derivatives. 48-hour rule. Skill or flow.
why_matters: Most marketing teams produce one asset and use it once. Repurposing is the single highest-leverage use of AI in this function.
what_to_do: For every long-form asset (blog, webinar, podcast), the rule is: AI produces 5 derivatives within 48 hours (LinkedIn post, X thread, email snippet, sales one-pager, internal brief). Build a Claude Skill or n8n flow that does it.
how_to_know: Asset-to-derivative ratio rises to 5+ across every long-form piece for a month.

title: Run one campaign end-to-end with agents owning the seams
body: One campaign. Agent-owned seams. Five human gates.
why_matters: You have AI inside steps. The next jump is letting agents own the handoffs between steps.
what_to_do: Pick one campaign. Agents own: brief enrichment from past data, draft production, derivative generation, distribution scheduling, performance reporting. Humans own only strategy, approval, and exceptions.
how_to_know: The campaign ships in half the calendar time of the previous benchmark and humans only touched it at five named gates.

title: Run a 60-minute prompting clinic per week for the first month
body: Weekly clinic. One workflow. Four weeks.
why_matters: AI fluency in marketing is bimodal: a few are flying, most are not. A weekly clinic closes the gap quickly.
what_to_do: Block 60 minutes a week for a month. Each session: one workflow (research, outline, draft, edit, repurpose). Bring three good prompts. Have everyone try them on real work.
how_to_know: After four weeks every team member has a Project of their own and uses it daily.

title: Ship a Marketing AI Owner role with 50% time
body: AI Owner. 50% time. Quarterly review.
why_matters: You are past part-time AI work. A named Owner with real time is the difference between continued progress and plateau.
what_to_do: Promote or hire a Marketing AI Owner. 50% of week. Job: own the prompt library, the agents, the evals, the cross-team enablement. Quarterly review with the CMO.
how_to_know: Within a quarter the Owner has shipped one new agent and the team uses two new shared Projects.

title: Publish a one-page rule on AI disclosure
body: Disclosure rule. One page. Memorised.
why_matters: AI-generated marketing without a disclosure stance is a brand and regulatory risk. One page is enough.
what_to_do: Decide and publish: when AI use is disclosed (always for editorial, never for ad copy, etc.), what the language is, who approves exceptions. Brief the team once.
how_to_know: Every team member can recite the disclosure rule.

title: Add a fact-check step to every AI-drafted external asset
body: Fact-check step. Default in workflow.
why_matters: AI hallucinations in marketing show up as recalled stats and made-up quotes. A standard step catches them.
what_to_do: For every AI-drafted asset that goes external, the workflow includes a fact-check step: AI cites sources, a human verifies the top 3. Build it into the Project or Skill so it cannot be skipped.
how_to_know: In the next month, at least one fabricated stat is caught before publication.

title: Run a quarterly brand-voice eval on AI output
body: Voice eval. Quarterly. Deploy gate.
why_matters: Voice drift is the silent failure mode of AI marketing. An eval catches it before customers do.
what_to_do: Build a brand-voice eval set (10–20 prompts, scored by a human panel of 3). Run it quarterly against your active Projects and agents. Block changes that drop the score.
how_to_know: You catch one voice regression in the first quarter the eval runs.

title: Time five assets before and after AI for two weeks
body: Five asset types. Ten data points each. Two weeks.
why_matters: AI in marketing pays for itself fast, but only if you can show the time numbers.
what_to_do: Pick five recurring asset types. Time the next 5 of each, with and without AI. Publish the result internally.
how_to_know: You can produce a per-asset-type before/after time saved.

title: Run AI vs control campaigns for one quarter
body: Three controlled comparisons. One quarter.
why_matters: Most "AI lift" stats are unfalsifiable. A simple control gives you a number.
what_to_do: For your three priority content types, run AI-assisted and human-only versions in parallel for a quarter. Hold goals constant. Report engagement, conversion, time-to-publish.
how_to_know: You can show a credible per-type lift number to the CMO and the CFO.

title: Build a marketing AI scorecard the CMO reviews monthly
body: Monthly scorecard. CMO review. Budget defended.
why_matters: Marketing AI investments lose visibility at scale. A scorecard keeps the budget defendable.
what_to_do: Build a dashboard with: assets produced per FTE, time-to-publish, AI-assisted engagement vs control, cost per asset. Update monthly. Present at the marketing leadership meeting.
how_to_know: The CMO opens the scorecard before each leadership meeting without prompting.

title: Show one AI-built asset every team meeting
body: Five minutes. Weekly. Rotated.
why_matters: Demos beat decks. Build the habit cheaply.
what_to_do: In every weekly marketing meeting, one team member spends 5 minutes showing what they built with AI that week. Rotate ownership. Hold the slot for two months.
how_to_know: After two months the slot is the most-anticipated part of the meeting.

title: Pair a craft writer with the highest AI user as a co-leader
body: Pair. One campaign. One internal talk.
why_matters: The fastest way to get the team past the AI vs craft argument is to embody the resolution in two people working together.
what_to_do: Pair your best craft writer with the team member using AI most. Co-lead one campaign end-to-end. Have them present the process and result to the team.
how_to_know: After the pairing, the craft-vs-AI debate stops being a recurring argument.

title: Reorganise the team around the agent stack, not channels
body: Re-org. Agent-centric. Quarterly review.
why_matters: Channel-based marketing teams ossify around legacy formats. Agent-centric teams scale.
what_to_do: Re-cut the team: instead of "social manager, email manager, content manager", organise around agents and their owners (research agent, draft agent, distribution agent, analytics agent). Keep specialism but in service of the stack.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, you produce more output per FTE and team members report higher satisfaction.

title: Decide which AI features your product ships this quarter
body: One-page bet. Two features. Exec sign-off.
why_matters: Without a stated bet, every PR debate becomes an AI strategy debate.
what_to_do: Pick one or two AI features that ship to customers this quarter (smart search, summarisation, generation). Write a one-page bet: what it does, who it's for, the metric it moves. Get exec buy-in. Cut everything else.
how_to_know: Within two weeks the engineering team can name the two AI features in flight and everything not in scope.

title: Move from feature-by-feature to AI-platform thinking
body: Platform team. Shared spine. New features comply.
why_matters: You have multiple AI features in production. Each one is a different stack. Platform thinking is the next jump.
what_to_do: Stand up a small platform team (2–3 engineers). Job: own the model gateway, the eval harness, the prompt library, the observability stack. All product features go through it.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, every new AI feature is shipped on the platform, not as a one-off.

title: Make AI-first the default in roadmap reviews
body: Roadmap question. Forced written answer. Kill list.
why_matters: You have the platform. The next step is changing how the roadmap gets written so AI is the default option, not the exception.
what_to_do: Add a question to every roadmap review: "What does the AI-native version of this look like?". Force a written answer. Kill features that have a meaningfully better AI version not on the roadmap.
how_to_know: Within two quarters, more than half the roadmap is AI-native by default.

title: Catalogue the production data your AI features will use
body: Catalogue. Per-feature spec. Living document.
why_matters: AI features built without a data catalogue regress unpredictably the moment a schema changes upstream.
what_to_do: List every table, queue and event AI features will read or write. Note: schema, owner, refresh frequency, sensitivity. Put it in a single document. Update it when schemas change.
how_to_know: Within a fortnight every AI feature in flight has a one-page data spec attached.

title: Stand up a vector store and one good retrieval pipeline
body: Vector store. One pipeline. Proven win.
why_matters: AI features eating raw documents are slow and expensive. A vector store is the smallest thing that compounds.
what_to_do: Stand up Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, or Turbopuffer. Pick one product surface that needs retrieval. Build the ingestion + retrieval pipeline. Ship it.
how_to_know: In one product surface, retrieval-augmented answers measurably beat the non-RAG baseline.

title: Wire MCP servers for your top 3 internal data sources
body: Three MCP servers. Internal + external consumers.
why_matters: Your engineers and your customer-facing agents need the same internal context. MCP is the lowest-friction way to give it to both.
what_to_do: Pick the top 3 internal sources (Linear, GitHub, your application database, Sentry). Stand up MCP servers for each. Have one product feature and one internal Claude Code workflow consume them.
how_to_know: Within a quarter at least one customer-facing feature and one internal workflow read live state through MCP.

title: Roll out an internal model gateway and stop direct provider calls
body: Gateway. All traffic. No direct keys.
why_matters: Direct provider keys per service is a cost, security, and observability disaster waiting at the next audit.
what_to_do: Stand up a thin internal gateway (LiteLLM, Helicone, or a 200-line Cloudflare Worker). Every service calls models through the gateway. Centralise auth, rate limits, logging, and cost attribution.
how_to_know: Within a month, no service has a direct provider key in its env.

title: Stand up a prompt and pattern registry for the org
body: Registry. Versioned. Referenced in shipped code.
why_matters: Engineers reinvent the same prompt patterns weekly. A registry is the smallest thing that creates compounding.
what_to_do: Build a registry (could be a GitHub repo, could be a Notion DB) of approved prompts and patterns. Each entry: prompt, model, eval set, owner, version. Make it the default source for product features.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, every shipped AI feature references at least one registry entry.

title: Make Claude Code or Cursor the default editor for the team
body: One tool. Universal seats. Two-week ramp.
why_matters: AI-assisted coding is no longer optional. The team that adopts uniformly outpaces the team that does not by a margin that compounds.
what_to_do: Pick one (Claude Code preferred for agentic work, Cursor for traditional IDE flow). Buy seats for everyone. Run a one-hour onboarding. Set the expectation: this is the default.
how_to_know: Within two weeks, every engineer has a daily commit attributed to the assistant.

title: Adopt agentic flows for one engineering workflow this quarter
body: One workflow. Agentic. Sub-30min human.
why_matters: You have AI in the editor. The next leverage is letting it run multi-step jobs without you babysitting.
what_to_do: Pick one workflow (test generation, doc writing, dependency upgrades, on-call triage). Use Claude Code in agent mode (or a custom n8n flow). Let it run with a clear scope. Review weekly.
how_to_know: After a month, the workflow runs end-to-end with under 30 minutes of human time per instance.

title: Promote agents into your CI/CD pipeline
body: Three agents in CI/CD. Pass/fail rules. Quarter run.
why_matters: Agents that only run locally have a ceiling. Putting them in CI/CD is what makes them part of how the team ships.
what_to_do: Pick three CI/CD steps where agents add value (PR review, changelog generation, release notes, security scan). Add them as pipeline jobs with named owners and clear pass/fail rules. Run for a quarter.
how_to_know: After a quarter the agents have caught at least one bug or security issue that would have shipped.

title: Run a 90-minute Claude Code workshop for the whole team
body: One workshop. Real work. Self-built flows.
why_matters: Most engineers use AI tooling at 20% of its capability. A live session beats a doc.
what_to_do: Block 90 minutes. Walk through: agent mode, custom commands, MCP, Skills. Have everyone follow on real work. Ship the artefact.
how_to_know: Within two weeks every engineer has run an agent flow they wrote themselves.

title: Make eval-writing a standard engineering skill
body: Framework. Workshop. Required eval set.
why_matters: Engineers who can ship AI features but cannot write evals are shipping liabilities at scale.
what_to_do: Stand up an eval framework (Promptfoo, Inspect, or your own). Run a 2-hour workshop on writing evals. Make it the requirement: no AI feature ships without an eval set.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, every AI feature has an eval set checked in alongside the code.

title: Promote an Engineering AI Tech Lead with platform mandate
body: Tech Lead. 80% time. Platform improvement shipped.
why_matters: You have advanced practice but it's tribal. A named Tech Lead is what turns it into a team capability.
what_to_do: Promote your strongest practitioner. Mandate: own the platform spine, the eval harness, the prompt registry, the agent patterns. 80% time. Quarterly review with the VP Engineering.
how_to_know: Within a quarter the Tech Lead has shipped one platform improvement adopted by every other team.

title: Publish three rules for AI in customer-facing features
body: Three rules. Memorised. Enforced by review.
why_matters: Engineers will ship AI features faster than your governance team can write a policy. Three clear rules close the gap.
what_to_do: Write three rules: what data the model never sees (PII, secrets, customer content unless contracted), what gets logged (every prompt, every output), what gets human-reviewed before shipping (anything that takes a destructive action).
how_to_know: Every engineer can recite the three rules.

title: Add prompt and output logging to every production AI call
body: Gateway logs. Queryable. Weekly review.
why_matters: Without logging you cannot debug, you cannot evaluate, and you cannot defend yourself in an incident.
what_to_do: Add structured logging at the gateway: prompt, model, output, latency, cost, user. Make it queryable. Run a weekly review of error rates and outliers.
how_to_know: Within a month you can answer "what did our AI do for user X yesterday" in under a minute.

title: Run weekly evals as a deploy gate on every customer-facing AI feature
body: CI evals. Deploy gate. Nightly prod runs.
why_matters: Evals at deploy time are the only credible answer to "is this safe to ship". Weekly is the floor.
what_to_do: Wire evals into the CI/CD pipeline. Define a baseline score per feature. Block deploys that drop more than 2 percentage points without explicit approval. Run nightly on prod.
how_to_know: In the first quarter, at least one regression is caught before it reaches a customer.

title: Track AI-assisted PR throughput per engineer
body: PR throughput. AI-attributed. Monthly compare.
why_matters: Without a number, AI tooling investment is unjustifiable to Finance the moment they ask.
what_to_do: Instrument: PR count per engineer per week, AI-assisted ratio (commits with assistant context), time-to-merge. Compare against the pre-rollout baseline.
how_to_know: You can show a credible per-engineer productivity delta inside a month.

title: Build an AI feature scorecard the product team reviews monthly
body: Per-feature scorecard. Monthly. Roadmap input.
why_matters: AI features regress quietly. A scorecard is what makes the regression a noticeable event.
what_to_do: For each shipped AI feature, track: usage, quality (eval scores), cost per call, latency, customer satisfaction proxy. Update monthly. Review at product leadership.
how_to_know: Product leadership cites the scorecard in their next roadmap discussion.

title: Make cost-per-call a standing engineering metric
body: Cost per call. Targets. Quarterly optimisation.
why_matters: At your scale, AI cost is a P&L line. Treating it like a normal engineering performance metric is what keeps it in budget.
what_to_do: Wire cost-per-call into the model gateway. Surface it per feature, per team. Set targets. Review quarterly. Optimise the worst offenders.
