how_to_know: Within two quarters, cost-per-call has dropped meaningfully on at least one feature without quality regression.

title: Run a Friday "AI build" session every week for a month
body: Friday slot. Four weeks. Demo at end.
why_matters: Engineers learn by building. A standing session beats any offsite.
what_to_do: Block Friday afternoon for four weeks. Each session: pick something small (an internal tool, a personal automation, a code review agent). Build it with AI. Demo at the end.
how_to_know: After four weeks, every engineer has shipped one self-built AI artefact.

title: Make AI-assisted PRs the visible default in code review
body: Senior credit. Normalised in PR descriptions.
why_matters: If the strongest engineers don't mention their assistant in PRs, the rest will keep hiding theirs.
what_to_do: Ask senior engineers to credit their assistant in PR descriptions ("agent drafted, I refined", "reviewed with Claude Code"). Make it normal. Stops the AI-as-shameful-shortcut framing.
how_to_know: Within a month, AI assistance is mentioned in more than half of PRs.

title: Reorganise teams around the platform stack
body: Platform team. Feature pods. Faster ship.
why_matters: Feature teams that don't share platform components reinvent everything. Reorganising around the stack is what unlocks the next gain.
what_to_do: Reorg into platform team + feature pods. Platform owns: gateway, evals, prompt registry, agent patterns. Pods own: features. Pods consume the platform; platform invests in what pods need.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, time-to-ship a new AI feature drops measurably.

title: Pick three People processes AI rebuilds first
body: Three processes. AI spine. 90-day commit.
why_matters: People functions try to AI everything and end up doing nothing. Three named processes is the right scope.
what_to_do: Choose three (job descriptions, screening summaries, onboarding journeys, policy Q&A, performance review prep). Commit that AI is the spine of those three for the next 90 days.
how_to_know: Within six weeks the three processes are 50% faster and the team can name what changed.

title: Tie People AI bets to the workforce metrics the CFO already cares about
body: Per-bet metric. CFO-credible. Cull list.
why_matters: You have AI bets running in People but the CFO sees them as cost. Tie them to time-to-hire, retention, ramp time and they become investment.
what_to_do: List every active People AI bet. For each, name the workforce metric it should move. Drop the bets without a clear metric.
how_to_know: In your next meeting with Finance, the AI conversation is led by metrics not anecdotes.

title: Make AI a line item in the finance operating plan
body: High-maturity finance functions plan AI capacity (people, vendor spend, compute) the same way they plan headcount.
why_matters: Without a plan line, AI investment is invisible to the audit committee and gets cut first in downturns.
what_to_do: Add an AI capacity line to the annual operating plan with explicit ROI hurdle and reforecast quarterly.
how_to_know: AI line appears in board pack; reforecast cadence in place.

title: Define the People function's role in company-wide AI fluency
body: Mandate. Curriculum. First cohort.
why_matters: People at your scale either own AI fluency across the company or it falls into a vacuum. Pick the lane.
what_to_do: Write a one-page mandate: People owns the fluency curriculum, the certification, the hiring bar update. Get exec sign-off. Resource it.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, the curriculum is in market and the first cohort has graduated.

title: Get your handbook, policies, and FAQs into a Claude Project
body: Handbook in a Project. First-stop. Tracked.
why_matters: Half the People team's time goes to answering questions already answered in writing. Putting them in a queryable Project is the cheapest fix.
what_to_do: Pull together the handbook, top 50 FAQs, and current policies into a Claude Project. Make it the People team's default first stop. Track which questions get asked.
how_to_know: Within a month, 30% of internal People questions are answered from the Project first.

title: Connect your ATS and HRIS to your AI surface
body: ATS + HRIS piped. One use case. Hiring manager pull.
why_matters: AI in People without ATS and HRIS context is generic advice. With it, it's an assistant.
what_to_do: Set up the integrations (Workday, Greenhouse, BambooHR, Lattice). Pilot one use case: AI-prepared candidate summaries before each loop, drawn from ATS. Run for a month.
how_to_know: Hiring managers reference AI summaries in debrief unprompted.

title: Build a People evidence layer agents read across hiring, performance, and engagement
body: Evidence layer. Manager-prep agent. Quality A/B.
why_matters: People decisions across silos are slow. A unified evidence layer lets agents serve managers without 7 tabs.
what_to_do: Stand up a People data layer that pulls ATS, HRIS, performance and engagement nightly. Build one agent that prepares manager check-ins from it. Compare to manual prep.
how_to_know: Managers prefer the agent prep over manual within a quarter.

title: Sanction one AI assistant for People and brief the team
body: One tool. Onboarded. Audited.
why_matters: People data is sensitive. One sanctioned tool plus clear scope is the only safe baseline.
what_to_do: Buy Claude Teams or ChatGPT Teams. Onboard the People team in one session. Publish: this is the only sanctioned account for any People data.
how_to_know: Within two weeks every People team member can show their last 10 prompts on the sanctioned account.

title: Stand up a People agent platform with HR-specific guardrails
body: People platform. Migrated. Direct access killed.
why_matters: Generic AI tools hit a ceiling in People because of sensitivity. A People-specific platform with the right guardrails is what lets you scale.
what_to_do: Build (or buy) a People agent platform that enforces redaction, role-based access, and audit trails. Migrate the most-used Projects to it. Decommission the duplicates.
how_to_know: Within a quarter, every People-data agent runs on the platform with zero direct provider access.

title: Make AI the first draft for every JD and offer letter
body: JD + offer Projects. AI first draft. Two-month hold.
why_matters: JD and offer letter cycle time is the easiest People AI win. Refusing it is just slower hiring.
what_to_do: Standardise: every JD and offer letter starts as an AI draft using the brand voice + role context. Build a Project for each. No exceptions for two months.
how_to_know: Time from request to first draft drops by 60% within a month.

title: Rebuild onboarding as an agent-prepared journey
body: Joiner pack agent. Five-hire pilot.
why_matters: Onboarding admin is the highest-volume, lowest-judgement work the People team does. The first agent should live here.
what_to_do: Build a journey agent that prepares the joiner pack: welcome doc, calendar invites, system access, first-week reading. Hiring manager approves once. Run for the next 5 hires.
how_to_know: Onboarding admin time drops by at least 50% across the next 5 hires.

title: Run hire-to-onboard as an agent-orchestrated pipeline
body: Pipeline agent. One role family. 10-hire run.
why_matters: You have agents in steps. The next move is letting them own the handoffs across recruiting, IT, manager prep, and People ops.
what_to_do: Pick one role family. Map the full hire-to-onboard flow. Hand orchestration to a single agent stack with clear named human gates. Run for 10 hires.
how_to_know: Time-to-productive drops measurably across the 10 hires versus the previous baseline.

title: Run a 60-minute People AI baseline session this month
body: One session. Three Projects. Two adopters.
why_matters: Most People teams have one person experimenting and the rest watching. One session moves the median.
what_to_do: Block 60 minutes for the People team. Show the sanctioned tool, the JD Project, the policy Project, and the rules. Have everyone try them on real work.
how_to_know: Within two weeks, two team members have built or used a Project in their daily work.

title: Train hiring managers in AI-assisted hiring
body: 90-minute manager training. Quarterly. Year-long.
why_matters: AI in hiring lives or dies on what hiring managers actually do. Train them, not just the recruiters.
what_to_do: Run a 90-minute session per leadership team: how to use AI for JD review, candidate prep, debrief synthesis. Make it a quarterly cadence for the next year.
how_to_know: In the next debrief round, hiring managers reference AI-prepared candidate notes by reflex.

title: Map finance AI use cases to SOX and ICFR controls
body: Any AI in a SOX-relevant process must be mapped to a control with evidence of operating effectiveness.
why_matters: Auditors will ask. If you cannot answer, expect a deficiency.
what_to_do: Inventory AI uses in SOX-relevant processes; map each to a control activity; document evidence collection.
how_to_know: Inventory complete; auditor walkthrough passes without findings.

title: Promote a People AI Lead with mandate to ship
body: People AI Lead. 50% time. Quarterly review.
why_matters: You are past part-time AI work. A named Lead with budget and time is what produces the next phase.
what_to_do: Promote or hire a People AI Lead. 50% of week. Job: own the People agent stack, the prompt library, the manager training, the People data layer. Quarterly review with the CHRO.
how_to_know: Within a quarter the Lead has shipped one new agent and one team-wide capability.

title: Publish three rules for AI in People processes
body: Three rules. One brief. Memorised.
why_matters: A short, clear set of rules beats a long policy nobody reads.
what_to_do: Write three rules: where AI is sanctioned (drafting, summarising), where it is not (screening decisions, comp decisions, terminations), what gets logged. Brief the team once.
how_to_know: Every People team member can recite the three rules.

title: Document where AI touches every hiring and performance decision
body: AI-in-People map. SAR-ready. Briefed.
why_matters: Regulators and candidates are starting to ask. Document it now or rebuild it later.
what_to_do: Map every step in hire-to-promote where AI is involved. For each, note: what it does, what is logged, what a candidate or employee can request. Publish internally. Brief the People team.
how_to_know: You can answer a Subject Access Request about AI use in any active candidate's journey within 24 hours.

title: Stand up a quarterly bias and quality review on People AI agents
body: Quarterly review. Bias check. One-page summary.
why_matters: Bias risk in People AI is real and material. Quarterly review with named owners is the minimum credible cadence.
what_to_do: Stand up a 60-minute quarterly review with the CHRO, Legal, and the People AI Lead. Agenda: agent outputs reviewed for bias, near-miss incidents, policy updates. Publish a one-page summary.
how_to_know: Every senior People leader has read the last quarterly summary.

title: Measure time-to-fill before and after AI on one role family
body: One role family. 20 data points.
why_matters: AI in People is easy to claim, hard to evidence. One role family is the right unit to measure.
what_to_do: Pick one role family. Measure the last 10 hires' time-to-fill. Run any AI move (JD agent, candidate prep). Measure the next 10. Publish the difference.
how_to_know: You can show a credible per-role-family time-to-fill delta.

title: Build a People AI scorecard the CHRO reviews monthly
body: Monthly scorecard. People leadership. Exec citation.
why_matters: People AI investments lose visibility at the CHRO level. A scorecard keeps the budget defendable.
what_to_do: Build a dashboard with: time-to-fill, time-to-onboard, JD cycle time, policy questions deflected, AI-assisted vs control on each. Update monthly. Present at People leadership.
how_to_know: The CHRO references the scorecard in their next exec update.

title: Tie one AI initiative to a workforce ROI number on the company OKRs
body: One bet. One company OKR. Quarterly report.
why_matters: People AI work earns a permanent place on the OKRs only when it is tied to a number leadership tracks anyway.
what_to_do: Pick the highest-leverage People AI bet. Tie it to a metric on the company OKRs (retention, ramp time, cost per hire). Publish the link. Report quarterly.
how_to_know: In the next OKR review the bet is discussed using the company metric.

title: Demonstrate AI in the next All-Hands People update
body: Five-minute demo. Specific. Manager pull-through.
why_matters: People as a function is read for what it models. Demoing AI in the next All-Hands changes the company default.
what_to_do: In your next People All-Hands slot, spend 5 minutes demoing one People AI use. Be specific. Show the work, not the tool.
how_to_know: Within a fortnight, two managers ask the People team for help with their own AI use.

title: Make AI fluency a hiring criterion for every people manager role
body: JD update. Interview question. Briefing.
why_matters: You set the bar for the next decade with the next 20 manager hires. AI fluency is now table stakes.
what_to_do: Update every manager-level JD: AI fluency is a stated requirement. Add a question to interviews. Brief hiring managers on what good looks like.
how_to_know: In the next manager hiring round, every offer goes to a candidate who can demo AI fluency.

title: Add AI fluency to every performance review
body: Review template. Manager training. Calibration input.
why_matters: You change behaviour at scale by changing what gets reviewed. AI fluency in reviews is the structural lever.
what_to_do: Add an AI-use question to every quarterly review template. Train managers in how to assess it. Make it part of the calibration conversation.
how_to_know: In the next review cycle, AI use is discussed in every review across the company.

title: Set a finance AI mandate tied to close cycle and forecast accuracy
body: Anchor AI in finance to two measurable KPIs the CFO already cares about: days-to-close and forecast variance.
why_matters: Without a mandate, finance AI becomes a parade of pilots with no P&L impact.
what_to_do: Draft a one-page mandate naming sponsor, two target KPIs, in-scope processes (close, FP&A, AP/AR), and out-of-scope (statutory filings).
how_to_know: Mandate signed by CFO; KPIs baselined; review cadence set.

title: Move from pilot list to a finance AI portfolio with stage gates
body: Treat AI initiatives as an investment portfolio with explicit stage gates and kill criteria.
why_matters: Mid-tier finance teams accumulate 8-12 pilots that never industrialise.
what_to_do: Categorise active pilots into Discover/Pilot/Scale/Sunset; require ROI and control evidence to advance each gate.
how_to_know: Portfolio reviewed monthly; at least one initiative scaled or sunset per quarter.

title: Establish a single chart-of-accounts mapping for AI use cases
body: Most finance AI failures trace back to inconsistent COA mappings between source systems and the GL.
why_matters: Without a canonical mapping, every model produces a different "revenue" number.
what_to_do: Document the canonical COA, source-to-GL mappings, and exception handling in a single place owned by the controller.
how_to_know: Mapping document published; reconciliation variance under 1%.

title: Build a finance data mart for AI consumption
body: Stop pointing models at the production ERP. Create a curated, audited mart with lineage.
why_matters: Direct ERP access creates performance and audit risk; marts give you control points.
what_to_do: Stand up a finance mart (warehouse schema) covering GL, AP, AR, with documented lineage and refresh SLAs.
how_to_know: Mart in production; at least two AI use cases consuming it; refresh SLA met >95%.

title: Treat finance data products as audited assets
body: Each finance data product (e.g. revenue-by-segment) gets an owner, SLA, and audit trail like a financial control.
why_matters: At scale, undocumented data products become the next material weakness.
what_to_do: Publish a finance data product catalogue with owner, SLA, lineage, and SOX/ICFR mapping for each.
how_to_know: Catalogue exists; data products mapped to controls; auditor signs off on lineage evidence.

title: Pick one enterprise AI assistant and ban shadow tools in finance
body: Sensitive financial data leaking into consumer chatbots is the #1 finance AI risk.
why_matters: Shadow tools create disclosure, contract, and IP risk that surfaces during audit.
what_to_do: Choose one enterprise-licensed assistant (e.g. Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise), publish an allow-list, and revoke shadow access.
how_to_know: Allow-list published; shadow tool usage drops to zero in DLP logs.

title: Deploy AI inside the close and consolidation tool, not alongside it
body: Bolt-on AI tools create reconciliation work. Use AI features inside your close platform (BlackLine, FloQast, Workiva).
why_matters: Standalone AI in finance creates a second source of truth that auditors will challenge.
what_to_do: Enable native AI features in your close platform; retire any standalone reconciliation copilots.
how_to_know: Native AI features live for at least 2 close cycles; standalone tools retired.

title: Run finance agents on a governed orchestration layer
body: Move from individual copilots to multi-step agents (e.g. variance investigation) on a governed runtime with full audit logs.
why_matters: Agentic finance work without governance is uninsurable and unauditable.
what_to_do: Stand up an agent runtime (e.g. internal platform on Bedrock/Vertex) with policy, logging, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
how_to_know: At least one finance agent in production with full audit trail and HITL gates.

title: Use AI to draft variance commentary for the monthly pack
body: Variance commentary is repetitive, well-bounded, and high-value. It is the right first workflow.
why_matters: Quick win that frees FP&A analysts from drafting and lets them focus on insight.
what_to_do: Pilot AI-drafted variance commentary for one BU for two close cycles; analyst reviews and edits before publication.
how_to_know: Commentary draft time cut by 50%+; analyst satisfaction up.

title: Embed AI in AP invoice triage and exception handling
body: AP is high-volume and rules-based — perfect for AI triage with human review on exceptions only.
why_matters: Frees AP team from low-value matching; reduces late-payment penalties.
what_to_do: Deploy AI invoice extraction and matching for one entity; route exceptions to humans; measure straight-through processing rate.
how_to_know: STP rate >70%; cycle time cut by 40%; no increase in duplicate payments.

title: Run continuous close with AI-driven anomaly detection
body: Move from periodic close to continuous close where AI flags anomalies in near-real-time.
why_matters: Continuous close compresses days-to-close and surfaces issues before they become restatements.
what_to_do: Deploy anomaly detection on GL postings with thresholds owned by controllers; integrate alerts into close workflow.
how_to_know: Days-to-close cut by 30%+; anomalies surfaced pre-close, not post-close.

title: Run a finance-specific AI fluency programme, not generic training
body: Generic AI training does not stick. Finance teams need scenarios using their actuals, their pack, their tools.
why_matters: Without context, training rarely changes daily behaviour.
what_to_do: Build a 4-week programme using anonymised real finance scenarios (variance, accruals, AP exceptions); measure pre/post usage.
how_to_know: Active weekly use rises from <20% to >60% of finance team.

title: Certify a finance AI champion in each sub-function
body: Champions sit inside FP&A, controllership, AP/AR, treasury — they translate use cases and unblock peers.
why_matters: Central enablement teams cannot scale; champions can.
what_to_do: Identify and certify one champion per sub-function; give them 10% time and a community of practice.
how_to_know: Champion network meets monthly; backlog of use cases grows organically.

title: Embed prompt and agent design into the finance career ladder
body: Make AI fluency a promotion criterion the same way Excel was 20 years ago.
why_matters: Without ladder integration, fluency stays optional and uneven.
what_to_do: Update finance role profiles (analyst, manager, director) with explicit AI competencies; train managers to assess.
how_to_know: Role profiles updated; AI competencies appear in performance reviews.

title: Publish a finance AI acceptable use policy
body: A short, finance-specific policy beats a generic enterprise policy nobody reads.
why_matters: Without it, you cannot enforce or audit anything.
what_to_do: Draft a 1-page policy covering allowed tools, data classifications, prohibited uses (audit working papers, MNPI), and review cadence.
how_to_know: Policy signed by CFO and CISO; acknowledged by 100% of finance.

title: Run a model risk management process for material finance AI
body: Adopt SR 11-7-style MRM for material models: validation, monitoring, challenger models, governance committee.
why_matters: Material models without MRM are a regulatory and reputational time bomb.
what_to_do: Establish MRM committee; classify models by materiality; require validation and monitoring for high-materiality models.
how_to_know: MRM committee active; validation reports for all high-materiality models.

title: Baseline three finance KPIs before deploying any AI
body: You cannot prove AI ROI without a clean before-picture.
why_matters: Without baselines, every benefit claim is contestable.
what_to_do: Baseline days-to-close, forecast variance, and FP&A analyst hours-on-commentary for 2 cycles before deployment.
how_to_know: Baselines documented and signed off by controller and FP&A lead.

title: Run quarterly AI value reviews with the CFO
body: Quarterly reviews force teams to convert activity into measured outcomes.
why_matters: Without rhythm, reporting drifts to vanity metrics (logins, prompts).
what_to_do: Establish a quarterly review pack: KPI deltas vs baseline, costs, risks, decisions to scale or sunset.
how_to_know: Pack reviewed quarterly; at least one decision to scale or sunset per review.

title: Tie finance AI investment to risk-adjusted NPV in capital allocation
body: Treat AI like any other capital decision: NPV with explicit risk adjustment for model and adoption risk.
why_matters: Without this discipline, AI spend grows faster than its measured return.
what_to_do: Build an NPV template with adoption-risk and model-risk discount factors; require for any AI investment >£100k.
how_to_know: Template in use; capital committee signs off on AI investments using it.

title: Make AI usage visible in finance team rituals
body: Lightweight rituals (Friday demo, Slack #wins) normalise AI use and reduce stigma.
why_matters: Without visibility, adoption stays hidden and uneven.
what_to_do: Add a 10-minute AI demo slot to the weekly finance team meeting; rotate presenters.
how_to_know: Demo slot active 8 weeks running; participation broadens beyond early adopters.

title: Reward shared prompts and templates, not individual heroics
body: A library of vetted finance prompts and templates compounds; individual hacks do not.
why_matters: Without sharing, the same wheel gets reinvented in every sub-function.
what_to_do: Stand up a shared prompt library with review process; recognise contributors in performance reviews.
how_to_know: Library has >50 vetted prompts; usage tracked and growing.

title: Hire and promote for AI-native finance ways of working
body: At maturity, AI fluency is non-negotiable. Hiring and promotion criteria reflect that.
why_matters: Without this, the function decays as senior leaders without fluency block change.
what_to_do: Update job specs and promotion criteria across finance to require demonstrated AI fluency; train interviewers to assess.
how_to_know: Job specs updated; interviewer calibration done; promotion panels apply criteria.

title: Anchor an Ops/CS AI mandate to deflection and CSAT
body: A focused mandate on ticket deflection and CSAT prevents AI in support from drifting into vanity automation.
why_matters: Without focus, AI in support multiplies channels and metrics without moving the customer experience.
what_to_do: Write a one-page mandate naming sponsor, two KPIs (deflection rate, CSAT), in-scope channels, and out-of-scope (T&S, billing disputes).
how_to_know: Mandate signed by COO/CCO; KPIs baselined; review cadence agreed.

title: Move from chatbot pilots to a tiered Ops/CS AI portfolio
body: Treat AI initiatives across support, success, and ops as a portfolio with stage gates and clear ownership.
why_matters: Most CS teams have 3-5 disconnected pilots that compete for the same agents and customers.
what_to_do: Map active initiatives across deflection, agent assist, success motions; assign owners and stage gates.
how_to_know: Portfolio reviewed monthly; duplicate pilots consolidated or sunset.

title: Make AI a strategic lever in the customer operating model
body: Stop treating AI as efficiency theatre. Use it to redesign tiers, segmentation, and the SLA promise itself.
why_matters: Marginal automation hits a ceiling. Redesign unlocks the next 10x.
what_to_do: Redesign customer tiers and SLAs assuming AI deflects 50%+ of L1, freeing humans for complex work.
how_to_know: New tier model live; SLA improves while cost-to-serve falls.

title: Consolidate ticket and conversation data into one searchable corpus
body: AI in support is only as good as the conversation history it can search.
why_matters: Without consolidation, models miss context and customers repeat themselves.
what_to_do: Centralise tickets, chats, calls (transcribed) into one indexed store with PII redaction.
how_to_know: Single corpus searchable; PII redaction verified; retention policy applied.

title: Build a customer-360 feature store for support and success AI
body: A shared feature store (entitlements, health score, past issues) prevents every model from rebuilding the same context.
why_matters: Without it, churn models, deflection bots, and CSM tools all reinvent the customer record.
what_to_do: Stand up a feature store covering entitlements, health, sentiment, and incident history with documented SLAs.
how_to_know: Feature store in production; consumed by at least two AI use cases.

title: Treat support knowledge as a product with versioning and SLAs
body: Knowledge bases that feed AI need product ownership, freshness SLAs, and review workflows — not a wiki.
why_matters: Stale KBs poison every downstream AI answer.
what_to_do: Appoint a knowledge product owner; define freshness SLAs by article class; instrument review workflow.
how_to_know: KB freshness SLA met >95%; AI answer accuracy improves quarter-on-quarter.

title: Turn on native AI in your existing helpdesk before buying new
body: Zendesk, Intercom, Salesforce, HubSpot all ship native AI. Use that before adding a third-party copilot.
why_matters: Adding tools creates integration debt; native features ship faster and stay aligned.
what_to_do: Audit native AI features in your existing helpdesk; enable agent assist and reply suggestions on one queue.
how_to_know: Native features live on at least one queue for 30 days; baseline metrics captured.

title: Deploy a deflection bot grounded in your knowledge base, not the open web
body: A grounded bot that says "I do not know" beats an open chatbot that hallucinates entitlements.
why_matters: Hallucinated answers in support create real liability and erode trust fast.
what_to_do: Deploy a RAG-grounded bot on one product area; require citations; route confidently to human on low confidence.
how_to_know: Bot live; >70% of answers cited; CSAT on bot conversations matches or beats human baseline.

title: Run multi-channel agents that resolve tickets end-to-end
body: Move from suggest-only copilots to agents that take action (refund, replace, escalate) with policy and HITL.
why_matters: End-to-end resolution is where the cost-to-serve curve breaks.
what_to_do: Stand up an agent runtime with policy, action allow-list, and HITL checkpoints for high-impact actions.
how_to_know: At least one agent resolving tickets end-to-end with audit trail; resolution time cut by 60%+.

title: Embed AI summaries at ticket close and case handoff
body: A short, structured summary at every close compounds into searchable history that future AI can use.
why_matters: Free-form notes are the #1 reason support AI underperforms long-term.
what_to_do: Make AI-generated summaries mandatory at ticket close and shift handoff; agents edit before saving.
how_to_know: Summary present on >95% of closed tickets; quality sampled weekly.

title: Run AI-prepared QBRs and renewals for CSMs
body: CSMs spend 30%+ of pre-meeting time stitching data. AI can pre-build the deck and talk track.
why_matters: Frees CSM time for the conversation that actually drives renewal.
what_to_do: Pilot AI-prepared QBR packs for one CSM segment; CSM reviews and edits; track time saved and renewal rates.
how_to_know: Prep time cut 50%+; CSM NPS on tooling improves.

title: Deploy proactive success motions triggered by AI signals
body: Move from reactive support to AI-triggered proactive motions (usage drop, sentiment shift, integration error).
why_matters: Proactive motions move CS from cost centre to retention engine.
what_to_do: Define 3-5 trigger types; build playbook for each; route signals to CSMs with recommended actions.
how_to_know: Triggers live; at least 30% of churn-risk accounts engaged before contract event.

title: Train support agents in human-in-the-loop, not prompt engineering
body: Agents do not need prompt theory; they need to know when to trust, when to edit, and when to override AI.
why_matters: Generic prompt training does not change behaviour at the desk.
what_to_do: Run a 2-hour HITL workshop using real tickets; measure pre/post override quality.
how_to_know: Override quality improves; AI suggestion acceptance lands in the healthy 50-75% band.

title: Certify CSMs in AI-assisted account planning
body: CSMs need fluency in using AI for account research, expansion plays, and renewal forecasting.
why_matters: Without fluency, AI tooling stays unused and CSMs revert to spreadsheets.
what_to_do: Build a CSM certification covering account research, expansion analytics, and renewal forecasting with AI.
how_to_know: All CSMs certified within 90 days; tool adoption >70% weekly.

title: Make AI fluency a leadership requirement across Ops/CS
body: Senior CS leaders without fluency block change. Make it a leadership development requirement.
why_matters: Without leadership fluency, transformation stalls at middle management.
what_to_do: Add AI fluency to leadership development programmes; require demonstrated use in promotion criteria.
how_to_know: All CS leaders certified; promotion panels apply criteria.

title: Publish a customer-facing AI disclosure
body: Customers increasingly expect to know when they are talking to AI. Disclosure builds trust and stays ahead of regulation.
why_matters: Hidden AI surfaces as a trust crisis the first time it goes wrong publicly.
what_to_do: Add a clear, plain-English disclosure to bot interactions and AI-generated emails; train agents to confirm if asked.
how_to_know: Disclosure live on all AI surfaces; customer feedback monitored.

title: Build an AI-incident runbook for support
body: When the bot says the wrong thing about pricing or policy, you need a runbook — not a Slack scramble.
why_matters: Without a runbook, small AI failures become public incidents.
what_to_do: Define incident classes (hallucination, escalation failure, PII leak), runbook for each, and post-incident review.
how_to_know: Runbook published; tested in tabletop exercise; reviewed quarterly.

title: Govern customer-facing agents under your existing T&S framework
body: Customer-facing agents need the same governance as content moderation: policy, red-teaming, review, appeals.
why_matters: Without T&S-grade governance, agents become a regulatory and reputational risk at scale.
what_to_do: Apply T&S framework to agents: policy, red-team, sample-review, appeals process, regulator engagement.
how_to_know: Framework applied; quarterly red-team and review reports published internally.

title: Baseline deflection, AHT, CSAT and FCR before any AI rollout
body: Without these four numbers from before, you cannot prove or defend AI value in support.
why_matters: Vendors and internal sponsors will both pressure you for impact stories — have receipts.
what_to_do: Capture 90 days of deflection, average handle time, CSAT, and first-contact resolution before turning anything on.
how_to_know: Baselines documented and signed off by support leadership.

title: Run a quarterly Ops/CS AI value review with the COO/CCO
body: Convert activity (sessions, prompts) into outcome (deflected tickets, retained ARR) every quarter.
why_matters: Without rhythm, vanity metrics dominate the narrative.
what_to_do: Build a quarterly review pack: KPI deltas, cost-to-serve, retention impact, decisions to scale or sunset.
how_to_know: Pack reviewed quarterly; at least one scale or sunset decision per review.

title: Tie AI investment in CS to net revenue retention
body: At maturity, the right CS metric for AI is NRR, not deflection. Optimise for retained and expanded revenue.
why_matters: Optimising for deflection alone risks under-serving accounts that drive expansion.
what_to_do: Re-orient AI investment cases around NRR impact; build attribution model linking AI motions to retention and expansion.
how_to_know: NRR-linked attribution in place; investment committee uses it.

title: Run a weekly AI wins-and-misses session for support
body: 15 minutes a week to share what worked and what failed builds psychological safety and accelerates learning.
why_matters: Without it, agents hide AI failures and stop using it.
what_to_do: Add a weekly 15-minute slot; rotate facilitators; share anonymised wins and misses.
how_to_know: Session active 8 weeks running; participation broadens beyond team leads.

title: Recognise agents who improve AI prompts and KB articles
body: Agents who fix the system make AI better for everyone. Recognise it.
why_matters: Without recognition, system-improving work falls to whoever cares most until they burn out.
what_to_do: Add KB and prompt contributions to recognition programmes and performance reviews; track contribution leaderboard.
how_to_know: Contribution leaderboard active; KB freshness improves measurably.

title: Redesign the agent and CSM role around AI augmentation
body: At maturity, the role itself changes — agents become editors and exception handlers, CSMs become strategic advisors.
why_matters: Without role redesign, AI sits on top of legacy roles and value leaks out.
what_to_do: Rewrite role profiles, comp structures, and career ladders for the AI-augmented support and success org.
how_to_know: New role profiles live; comp aligned; career paths visible to staff.
